D001-D011_h001.question_both:
I’ve been feeling overwhelmed for a while now—probably the past few months, maybe longer. At work, I’m constantly moving, checking trucks, rerouting pickups, jumping from one thing to the next. My crew says I never slow down, like I’m always buzzing. Honestly, I don’t even realize I’m doing it until someone points it out.  

The problem is, I can’t seem to stick with one task long enough to finish it properly. I’ll start scheduling routes, then notice an email and switch, then remember a call I need to make and lose the thread. It’s not that I don’t care—I *do*—but my mind just pulls me in different directions. Even at home, my wife says I talk nonstop, mostly about little things—what needs fixing, what’s coming up, what went wrong that day.  

I get distracted easily, too. A noise outside, a thought about something from years ago—it just sneaks in. I don’t know if it’s stress or just how I’ve always been. I worry sometimes, sure, but mostly I just feel scattered. Not anxious exactly—just… never settled.
D001-D011_h001.question_a:
I’ve always felt like my brain never really shuts off, but not because I’m worried—more like it can’t settle on one thing. At work, I’ll start planning a route or writing a report, but halfway through, I notice I’ve gotten sidetracked by some unrelated thought or a noise outside, and the task’s left half-done. It’s been this way since I was a kid—my teachers said I was bright but couldn’t stick to one thing.  

I’m constantly moving—my wife says I’m like a wind-up toy. Even during dinner, I’m fidgeting, getting up to do something else, or talking non-stop about whatever pops into my head. I don’t mean to interrupt or dominate conversations, but the words just come out before I think.  

I do get anxious sometimes—deadlines, family stuff—but that’s not why my mind jumps around. The distraction happens even when I’m calm, especially if the task feels routine or boring. When something’s new or exciting, I hyperfocus for a while, then lose steam. It’s not the worry that breaks my focus—it’s the environment, a sound, or just a sudden idea. The restlessness? It’s like a constant hum I can’t turn down.
D001-D011_h001.question_b:
I’ve been feeling overwhelmed for about six months now. Work’s been the same as always—managing schedules, routes, inspections—but my mind just won’t settle. I’m constantly going over things: Did I miss a pickup? Was my report accurate? What if something goes wrong and someone gets hurt? It’s like my brain won’t shut off, even at home. My wife says I pace a lot, and I guess I do—I’m always moving, fidgeting, getting up from the table, starting one thing and jumping to another. I talk a lot too, especially when I’m nervous, which is pretty much all the time. 

The worst part is I can’t organize my thoughts or my days like I used to. I’ll sit down to plan the week and end up lost in a loop of “what ifs.” Little noises pull me in—phones ringing, trucks backing up—and I’ll start thinking about everything except what I’m doing. But it’s not that I’m bored or chasing something new; it’s that the worry hijacks me. I’m not impulsive—I’m careful, maybe too careful—but the anxiety makes me feel scattered, like I’m running on empty while my mind runs too fast.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder
